subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-account DM mode that routes user-authorized message.im events to an xoxp token and replies as that Slack user?
rationale: This changes Slack identity, authorization, and audit semantics; code inspection can show the missing path but cannot decide whether OpenClaw should allow regular-user impersonation as a product/security policy.

options.title: Approve default-off user-account mode
options.body: Implement a Slack plugin mode with explicit opt-in, authorization-to-token mapping, scope documentation, live Slack proof, and tests for bot-token behavior staying unchanged.

options.title: Keep Slack bot/app identity only
options.body: Close or defer the request and document that userToken remains for read operations and limited write fallback, not inbound user-account control.

options.title: Require external plugin first
options.body: Ask for a third-party or ClawHub Slack-user plugin experiment before changing the official Slack plugin security boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve default-off user-account mode
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack plugin mode with explicit opt-in, authorization-to-token mapping, scope documentation, live Slack proof, and tests for bot-token behavior staying unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack token/security and channel-boundary history makes this the best available owner signal for the policy choice.
